program_name: Master in Sound and Music Computing (SMC)

A software engineer is the archetypal applicant - the syllabus is DSP, machine learning for audio and audio software engineering, and the thesis is a music-tech artefact. Highest priority for manual verification in Wave 2.

program_name: Master in Human Interaction and Artificial Intelligence (MHIAI)

fit_notes: Maker-studio master where an engineer builds interactive AI-driven interfaces; a generative-music instrument or an adaptive-audio interface is a plausible final project. Engineering degrees are named explicitly in the admission text, so the 300-ECTS diploma clears the bar with room to spare. Cheapest of the Elisava options that is taught in English.

program_name: University Master in Interdisciplinary Design and Communication Studies (Master Universitario en Estudios Interdisciplinarios en Diseno y Comunicacion)

scholarship_names: Elisava Masters' Scholarships (1 x 50% reserved for this official master; next call March 2027)

fit_notes: The only Elisava route that ends in an OFFICIAL Spanish master's degree - materially better for the student visa and for any later PhD. Research-and-prototype structure (theoretical report + material prototype + scientific poster) suits an engineer who wants a documented music-interface artefact rather than a portfolio piece.

fit_notes: Generative-AI creative practice with an English-taught Barcelona cohort; a generative-music or AI-assisted production tool is an obvious final project for someone who can already code the models.

Portfolio is required but 'other profiles with a suitable portfolio' is explicit, so the in-progress music portfolio can carry the application. Strong for building interactive/immersive audio experiences.

program_name: Master Universitari en Estudis Avancats en Disseny - Barcelona (MBDesign), specialty Disseny, Innovacio i Tecnologia (Design, Innovation and Technology)
institution: Universitat Politecnica de Catalunya with Universitat de Barcelona

red_flags: Fees, deadlines and admission criteria not published on the pages opened this session - must be confirmed on the UPC master admissions portal. One of the five specialties is Industrial Design Engineering, so engineer intake is normal, but this is not stated as an explicit rule.

The Design, Innovation and Technology specialty is English-taught, and a 60-ECTS thesis year lets an engineer build and document a music-hardware or music-software product.

Worth one manual pass in Wave 2 before discarding.

institution: University of Twente
tuition_notes: Institutional (higher-rate) fee for non-EU/EEA students, EUR 21,700 for 2026-2027 (2025-2026 was EUR 18,900). 2027-2028 not yet published. February entrants pay 7/12 of the annual amount for the first period.
application_deadline: 1 April 2027 (scholarship deadline; programme admission deadline TBC)
deadline_source_cycle: 2027 cycle for scholarships (window 15 Oct 2026 - 1 Apr 2027 published); programme admission deadline 2027 TBC
entry_requirements_summary: Research-university bachelor in a related field; a pre-master exists for HBO applicants; international applicants pass an online eligibility check. September and February starts.
scholarship_names: University of Twente Scholarship (UTS); NL/Holland Scholarship (EUR 5,000 first year); Kipaji Scholarship
tunisia_eligible: likely - UTS and NL Scholarship are open to excellent students from non-EU/EEA countries; Tunisia not named on the pages opened
red_flags: Non-EU fee rose 15 percent in one year (18,900 to 21,700) - budget for a further rise in 2027-28. UTS is competitive and its deadline (1 April) precedes the usual admission deadline, so the scholarship drives the timetable.
fit_notes: The best pure fit on this path in the Netherlands for a software engineer: Interaction Technology is a technical HMI/affective-computing master with heavy prototyping (game-engine and XR development, experience design), taught in the Human Media Interaction group. It is also an EIT Digital HCID entry point, so the same application can open a double-degree route. A gesture/DJ-controller or adaptive-audio thesis sits naturally here.

institution: Delft University of Technology (Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering)
tuition_notes: Institutional rate for non-EU MSc students, EUR 25,633 for 2026-2027. A transitional rate of EUR 23,404 applies only to students already enrolled who paid EUR 22,290 in 2025-2026.
entry_requirements_summary: Separate admission tracks for Dutch BSc, Dutch HBO and non-Dutch university degrees; the detailed non-Dutch criteria page could not be opened this session. September start (February only for Dutch IDE BSc graduates).
scholarship_names: Justus and Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship (not verified this session)
red_flags: EUR 25,633/year is the highest non-EU fee found on this path - roughly EUR 51,000 over two years, so this is only viable with a full scholarship. IDE masters usually expect a design bachelor; a software-engineering entrant may face a bridging requirement. Admission-criteria page not reachable this session.
fit_notes: World-leading interaction-design faculty with prototyping labs and industry-brief projects; a music-interaction thesis (instrument, controller, listening experience) is entirely normal here. The client's 300-ECTS engineering diploma far exceeds the 180/240-ECTS entry bar, but the design-portfolio expectation is the real gate.

institution: Delft University of Technology (Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering)
tuition_notes: Institutional rate for non-EU MSc students, 2026-2027.
entry_requirements_summary: Separate criteria for Dutch BSc, HBO and non-Dutch degrees; September start.
red_flags: Same EUR 25,633 non-EU fee. Design-portfolio expectation not verified.
fit_notes: The hardware-leaning sibling of Design for Interaction: digital fabrication, computational design, smart materials and prototyping. This is the Delft route for someone who wants to build a physical music device (controller, synth, wearable) with an engineering-grade process behind it.

institution: Delft University of Technology (Faculty of Industrial Design Engineering)
tuition_notes: Institutional rate for non-EU MSc students, 2026-2027.
entry_requirements_summary: Separate criteria for Dutch BSc, HBO and non-Dutch degrees; September start.
red_flags: Same EUR 25,633 non-EU fee; least technical of the three Delft IDE masters.
fit_notes: Business models, innovation strategy and new-product development - the route for an engineer who wants to run a music-tech product line or start a venture rather than write the DSP. Pairs a strong technical CV with the commercial vocabulary the client currently lacks.

institution: Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e)
tuition_notes: Institutional fee for non-EU/EEA students: EUR 21,700 for 2026-2027 and EUR 22,400 for 2027-2028 (the 2027-28 figure is published).
deadline_source_cycle: 2027-2028 fee published; application deadlines 2027 TBC. Departmental admissions board meets monthly October-July, so applying early matters.
entry_requirements_summary: Admission decided by the departmental Admissions Board on prior education, professional experience and skills gained elsewhere; only one mandatory course, the rest of the programme is self-composed.
red_flags: Non-EU fee for the client's actual intake year (2027-2028) is confirmed at EUR 22,400 - about EUR 44,800 over two years without a scholarship. Admission is board-discretionary rather than rule-based, which cuts both ways.
fit_notes: Almost entirely self-directed: one mandatory course and a portfolio of squads/projects the student defines, in a department built around intelligent interactive systems and making. That structure is ideal for someone who wants two years of building music-tech artefacts inside a technical university while keeping a DJ/production practice running.

program_name: MSc Creative Intelligence and Technology (formerly MSc Media Technology)
institution: Leiden University (LIACS with the Academy of Creative and Performing Arts)
tuition_notes: Non-EU institutional fee not reachable on the pages opened this session.
entry_requirements_summary: Welcomes applicants from diverse educational backgrounds and states it is open to any field of previous bachelor education; students bring their own research question and work by making. September and February starts.
scholarship_names: Leiden University Excellence Scholarship (LExS) - not verified this session
red_flags: Fees, deadlines and the concrete admission rule set were not obtainable from the pages opened. Programme was renamed from Media Technology, so older sources use the old name.
fit_notes: Explicitly a science-by-doing master run jointly by the computer-science institute and the arts academy: students propose their own creative-technology research and build it. Historically the Dutch home of music-technology and sound-installation theses, and one of the very few masters that says outright it accepts any bachelor background - an unusually low-friction entry for a software engineer with a music question.

program_name: Master of Music - pathway Music Design
institution: HKU University of the Arts Utrecht (Music and Technology)

Round 1 is motivation letter, study plan, CV and portfolio; shortlisted candidates get an online interview.

tunisia_eligible: yes - the NL Scholarship targets talented students from outside the EEA (Switzerland and Suriname excluded); Music Design is on the eligible-programme list
red_flags: Portfolio-gated: the client's music portfolio is still in progress and this is the binding constraint, not the academic record. Partly Dutch-language delivery. NL Scholarship deadline for the 2026-27 round was 1 May 2026, so the 2027 equivalent will fall around May 2027 - earlier than most admission deadlines.
fit_notes: The clearest music-technology-plus-design master in the Netherlands, and the only one found where a named EUR 5,000 scholarship is confirmed open to a Tunisian applicant. HKU explicitly admits candidates without a Bachelor of Music, so the 300-ECTS engineering diploma plus a strong producer portfolio is a real route. Directly serves the dual software-engineer / electronic-producer ambition.

program_name: Master Digital Design - track Interaction Design
institution: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (AUAS/HvA)
tuition_notes: Non-EU institutional fee not published on the pages opened; page states an extra ~EUR 800/year for books and materials on top of the annual tuition fee.
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree plus demonstrated previous design experience via an annotated portfolio; limited places with a selection procedure. Built with nine Dutch design agencies (Mirabeau, Fabrique, DEPT, Media.Monks, Momkai and others); team projects with real client briefs.
red_flags: Annotated design portfolio is a hard eligibility criterion and places are capped by selection - the weakest point for a candidate whose portfolio is code, not design artefacts. Fees not published on the pages opened.
fit_notes: One intense year in Amsterdam (the client's top-priority city) inside a studio co-owned by the leading Dutch digital agencies, with playgrounds in Emerging Interactions and Beyond-Human Design. For a software engineer this converts engineering skill into hireable product-design credibility fast, and Amsterdam is also the strongest electronic-music market in the region.

institution: Breda University of Applied Sciences (BUas)
tuition_notes: Page quotes EUR 2,694 for 2026-2027, which is the Dutch STATUTORY rate - the non-EEA institutional rate is not shown and will be substantially higher.
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor in Business Administration, Media Studies, Communication Studies, IT or a related media field. Four learning paths: applied R&D, media theory and technologies, industry case work with real clients (Samsung, KLM, Banijay, DPG Media, Google, NPO) and a graduation project combining thesis with a working prototype.
red_flags: The quoted EUR 2,694 is the statutory fee, NOT what a Tunisian national pays - the institutional non-EEA rate must be confirmed before this row is used for budgeting. Breda is outside the priority Amsterdam/Utrecht cluster.
fit_notes: IT is named explicitly among accepted bachelors, and the graduation project is thesis PLUS prototype - so a software engineer can ship a working media/music product as the degree deliverable, with named industry clients attached. A cheap, fast (60 ECTS, one year) product-innovation credential if the non-EU fee turns out to be moderate.

institution: Breda University of Applied Sciences (BUas)
tuition_notes: EUR 2,694 quoted for 2026-2027 (statutory rate); non-EEA rate not shown.
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor in a related field PLUS at least three to five years of equivalent industry experience; fully online, roughly 40 hours per week study load.
red_flags: Requires 3-5 years of industry experience, which a 2027 graduate does not have - likely ineligible until later. Fully online means NO Dutch student visa and no residence in Europe, which defeats the relocation goal.
fit_notes: Logged for completeness and as a fallback if the client works for several years first. Not a 2027 option: the experience bar and the absence of a visa route both rule it out for now.

institution: Utrecht University
tuition_notes: EUR 25,306 per year for non-EU/EEA students, 2026-2027.
entry_requirements_summary: Selective research master with separate criteria for Dutch research-university, Dutch HBO and non-Dutch bachelors; February and September starts.
scholarship_names: Utrecht Excellence Scholarship (not verified this session)
red_flags: EUR 25,306/year non-EU is near the top of the range. Selective research master - admission criteria for a non-Dutch engineering degree were not reachable this session. Utrecht's sibling MSc Game and Media Technology may be the better technical fit and should be checked in Wave 2.
fit_notes: Research-grade HCI at a top-50 university in Utrecht, in the same city as HKU - useful because the client could plausibly build a music-interaction thesis with HKU collaborators nearby. Strong for someone who wants the academic/research door left open rather than a studio credential.

institution: Universitaet der Kuenste Berlin jointly with Technische Universitaet Berlin
institution_type: Public university of the arts with a public technical university
language_of_instruction: TBC (programme materials in German and English; the English page directs readers to the German version for detail)
tuition_notes: No tuition fees at UdK/TU Berlin for any nationality; only the semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) applies - the exact 2027 amount was not confirmed on the pages opened.
deadline_source_cycle: Window 1 April - 15 May 2026 confirmed for winter semester 2026/27; the 2027/28 window is expected to mirror it but is TBC
entry_requirements_summary: First degree-qualifying university degree; bachelor graduates from design, art, ENGINEERING, natural sciences, humanities and social sciences are explicitly eligible. Application via the UdK/TU Berlin portal; a portfolio is referenced. Four-semester research-oriented programme.
scholarship_names: DAAD study scholarships (not verified this session)
red_flags: Language of instruction not confirmed in writing - the English UdK page pushes readers to the German version, so assume significant German exposure until proven otherwise. Portfolio/admission-test detail and the exact semester fee could not be opened (the UdK application-guide URL 404s and design-computation.berlin now redirects to newpractice.net). Very small, highly selective cohort.
fit_notes: Effectively free (no tuition, only a semester contribution of a few hundred euros) at two of Berlin's best institutions - the single strongest funding-first row on this path. Engineering graduates are named explicitly among eligible applicants, and the programme is built exactly on the design-plus-code intersection this client occupies. Berlin is also the world capital for electronic music, so a music-tech thesis has an unmatched surrounding scene.

program_name: Innovation Management, Entrepreneurship and Sustainability (IMES), M.Sc.
institution: Technische Universitaet Berlin
tuition_notes: No tuition; semester fee approximately EUR 360. If the second year is taken at the University of Twente under the double degree, additional Twente tuition applies.
deadline_source_cycle: Published as an annual pattern (early April to mid May) for the winter-semester intake; exact 2027 dates TBC
entry_requirements_summary: First university degree in economics/business administration, social sciences, ENGINEERING SCIENCES, natural sciences or a related programme; C1 English; restricted admission with 50 places, ranked by final grade plus up to 100 points for prior coursework in economics, methodology, sustainability, mathematics and statistics. Year 1 at TU Berlin (60 ECTS), year 2 abroad or flexible.
red_flags: Only 50 places and admission is ranked on the first-degree grade plus prior credits in economics, statistics and methodology - an engineering diploma scores on maths/statistics but may score zero on the economics component. Application window closes in mid-May, far earlier than Dutch deadlines.
fit_notes: English-taught, tuition-free, in Berlin, and engineering sciences are an explicitly named entry route - a rare combination for a funding-first strategy. It gives a software engineer the venture-building and innovation-management layer needed to take a music-tech product to market, and the year-two mobility option includes the University of Twente, which also hosts the Interaction Technology master on this same path.

institution: Technische Universitaet Berlin
tuition_notes: No tuition fees; semester contribution only (approx. EUR 360 at TU Berlin).
application_deadline: TBC - see TU Berlin central dates and deadlines page
entry_requirements_summary: First degree in digital media and technology or a related field INCLUDING at least 15 ECTS mathematics, 18 ECTS computer science, 24 ECTS media technology and 20 ECTS media communication; proof of German at the required level for holders of a foreign school-leaving certificate; English B2. The programme is admission-free (open admission).
red_flags: GERMAN-TAUGHT - tagged, not dropped, per brief; German proof is mandatory for applicants with a foreign school certificate. The hard credit prerequisites (24 ECTS media technology and 20 ECTS media communication) are the real obstacle: a software-engineering diploma clears maths and computer science easily but is unlikely to show 44 ECTS of media subjects.
fit_notes: Open admission (no numerus clausus) and zero tuition make this the cheapest technical media master in Berlin if the credit profile can be argued - audio/media-signal courses from the engineering diploma would need to be mapped onto the media-technology requirement. Worth a direct enquiry to the admissions office rather than a self-assessment.

program_name: Internationaler Studiengang Medieninformatik (International Media Informatics), M.Sc.
institution: HTW Berlin (Hochschule fuer Technik und Wirtschaft Berlin)
tuition_notes: Public Berlin university of applied sciences - no tuition fees; semester contribution only (amount not confirmed on the pages opened).
deadline_source_cycle: Annual pattern published on the official programme site without a year qualifier - confirm the 2027 dates before relying on them
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor with at least 180 credit points, comparable to HTW Berlin's International Media Informatics bachelor or a related programme. Specialisations: Game Technology and Interactive Systems, Visual Computing, Web Technology; two semesters of team practice projects (groups of 5-6) plus independent coursework; electives from applied computer science including Human-Computer Interaction and Mobile Computing.
red_flags: Requires the first degree to be comparable to HTW's own media-informatics bachelor - a general software-engineering diploma should qualify as related but this needs written confirmation. Duration and ECTS not stated on the programme pages. Both winter and summer starts, so a February 2027 or September 2027 entry are both possible.
fit_notes: Free, English-taught, in Berlin, with a two-semester group practice project and a Game Technology and Interactive Systems track - the closest thing Berlin has to a build-things media-tech master for a coder. Interactive-audio, generative-visuals and music-app projects fit the practice-project format directly, and the 180-CP bar is trivially cleared by a 300-ECTS diploma.

institution: CODE University of Applied Sciences Berlin
tuition_notes: EUR 1,250 per month on the Direct Pay model (about EUR 15,000 per year; roughly EUR 30,000 for the 120-ECTS track) or EUR 650 per month on the Stretch Pay model over double the period. No separate non-EU rate published - confirm with admissions.
application_deadline: 31 December 2026 for the Spring 2027 intake (semester starts 1 February 2027); 20 August 2026 for Fall 2026
deadline_source_cycle: 2026 and 2027 cycles both published; a Fall 2027 deadline is not yet listed
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor's degree IN ANY FIELD plus at least one year of professional experience after the bachelor (internships, working-student roles or founding a startup count); English B2; portfolio and motivational statement through the application portal, then an interview with faculty and admissions.
scholarship_names: CODE scholarships and grants, flexible payment plans, Income Share Agreements, KfW student loans
red_flags: Expensive for a private UAS (about EUR 30,000 for the two-year track) and the one-year-of-professional-experience rule is a hard gate for a 2027 graduate - internships or a startup do count, so this must be evidenced carefully. State recognition/accreditation was not confirmed on the pages opened; confirm before relying on it for the visa.
fit_notes: Project-based product school embedded in Berlin's startup scene, with any-field bachelors explicitly welcome and a Spring intake (1 February 2027) that fits an early-2027 move. Suits an engineer who wants to build and ship a music product with design and venture coaching rather than sit exams; portfolio-based admission also rewards the music work already in progress.

institution: CODE University of Applied Sciences Berlin
tuition_notes: Same fee model as the M.A.: EUR 1,250 per month Direct Pay or EUR 650 per month Stretch Pay.
application_deadline: 31 December 2026 for the Spring 2027 intake (starts 1 February 2027)
entry_requirements_summary: Bachelor in any field plus at least one year of post-bachelor professional experience; English B2; portfolio, motivational statement and interview.
scholarship_names: CODE scholarships and grants; Income Share Agreements; KfW loans
red_flags: Same cost and experience-gate caveats as N-026; accreditation status unconfirmed on the pages opened.
fit_notes: The engineering-leadership variant: keeps the technical core while adding product and business command. For a software engineer whose end state is CTO or founder of a music-tech company, this is the more natural of the two CODE degrees, and the one-year 60-ECTS option keeps total cost near EUR 15,000.

institution: UE University of Europe for Applied Sciences
institution_type: Private university of applied sciences (FIBAA accredited, system-accredited)

Third-party sources quote higher non-EU totals (about EUR 16,407 for the 2-semester fast track and EUR 19,782 for the 3-semester track, plus a EUR 3,000 deposit) - NOT confirmed on the official page, so the non-EU figure must be re-checked.
deadline_source_cycle: TBC - both winter and summer intakes exist
